title: No adversary-in-the-middle activity observed; network and logon evidence consistent with normal domain operations
summary: Across the Windows and Zeek windows there is no evidence of traffic interception. Sysmon EventCode=3 destinations are dominated by the domain controllers (192.168.0.4, 10.0.0.4) and local/loopback addresses, with the remainder being Microsoft/Office telemetry endpoints. The only NTLM network logon (4624, LogonType 3, NtLmSsp, NTLM V2) is pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local at 2020-05-01T23:20:41-04:00 from 172.18.39.2 with Workstation Name 10.0.1.4; 172.18.39.2 is the address newyork.dmevals.local's dns.exe forwards queries to (source.ip 10.0.0.4, source.port 53), i.e. the DC's own DNS forwarder path, not a relay. The real attacker activity in this window is lateral movement (PsExec service installs by pbeesly on nashua.dmevals.local followed by C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe), which is outside the T1557 family.

title: NBT-NS name queries and SMB sessions are routine domain traffic, not poisoning or relay

No relay tooling, no LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning script blocks (PowerShell search returned zero hits), and the 4697 service installs are PsExec (PSEXESVC) and normal svchost-based services, not relay tooling.
